effects.prompt: Search your deck for a Phoenix Flame?

_comment:
'When you attack with Flamecall Awakening, if you've played another red card this turn, you may search your deck for a Phoenix Flame, reveal it, put it into your hand, then shuffle.' Draconic Action - Attack (FaiBlitzDeck).

PRINTED GO AGAIN NOT AUTHORED: unconditional keyword line, fires from the card DB keywords field; re-authoring it would be a defect. Nothing gates it, so no SOURCE_IS_ATTACK conditional-keyword strip applies either.

COUNT=2 IS DELIBERATE: the 'play' turn event is recorded at announce (play.py:1085-1101, carrying the card's colour as a qualifier; _record_turn_event normalises it to did_this_turn:play:red, effect_keywords.py:597-605), while ON_ATTACK fires later at the Attack Step - so by trigger time Flamecall itself is already counted as one red card played. count>=2 therefore means exactly 'another red card this turn'. EVENT_THIS_TURN reads event/qualifier/count (condition_types.py:1070-1112).

OPTIONALITY: release note 3 says the whole triggered effect is optional - MAY (effect_types.py:3788-3856) offers the block and declining runs nothing, shuffle included. Release note 4 (fail-to-find still shuffles) is SEARCH_DECK's own behaviour: it calls effect_shuffle unconditionally after the choice loop (effect_types.py:1786-1815), chosen or not, and ask_optional gives the FAIL_TO_FIND sentinel.

NAME MATCH: SEARCH_DECK reads 'name' (effect_types.py:1721) and matches flattened-substring against the drawn card's name OR slug, so 'Phoenix Flame' hits phoenix_flame_red/yellow/blue. destination 'hand' is the handler default and is an explicit read param; searched cards move public (is_public=True) = the printed reveal. No token definitions needed - it only ever fetches real deck cards.
